enforced_by: the video edit's gate (cutsheet.py) refuses a caption look that is not a row
note: Caption looks — how the words on screen look and move. A setting, never a re-edit.

rows.name: Bold highlight
rows.what: Big white capitals with a black outline, 2–4 words at a time, the word being spoken turns yellow and pops.

rows.name: Clean lower
rows.what: Sentence-case white words on a soft dark plate, low in the frame. Reads like a subtitle, not a shout.

rows.name: One word
rows.what: One huge word at a time, dead centre. For hooks and fast cuts.

rows.name: Word box
rows.what: Bold white capitals, 2–3 words at a time; the word being sung or said sits on a coloured box that moves word to word.

rows.name: Edits glow
rows.what: Instagram's Edits-app caption preset, rebuilt: a heavy, tightly spaced grotesque for the plain words, the words each phrase turns on (the step's action, the ingredient, the payoff, the comment word — the kit's caption_accent) in a tall condensed serif italic about 1.4x bigger, a soft white glow on every letter, each word fading in on its own as it is said into a line already laid out (nothing shifts), up to 5 words, centred on the chest above what the person holds.
